packages.reason: All four nodes share the same essential nature: the domain of spiritual displacement rooted in loss of faith. In Torah #40, the Rebbe teaches that all travel (נסיעה וטלטול) IS corruption of faith (קלקול האמונה), and corruption of faith IS a bechina of idolatry (עבודת אלילים/עבודה זרה). The word 'צא' (go out/travel) in Isaiah 30:22 is explicitly cited in the context of idolatry and IS a bechina of travel and displacement. Thus: צא = נסיעה וטלטול = קלקול האמונה = עבודה זרה. These are not four different things linked by cause-and-effect — they are four facets of the same corrupted spiritual state: the state of a person who does not believe that God can provide everything he needs, and therefore leaves his place to seek his needs elsewhere. This is, in essence, what idolatry is: attributing one's provision to something other than God.

Travel (Component A) IS corruption of faith IS idolatry (Component B). Furthermore, the word 'צא' is cited from a verse explicitly about idolatry (Isaiah 30:22), making 'צא' a direct linguistic token of the idolatry domain. All four nodes are different expressions of the same underlying reality: the state of displaced-from-God spiritual existence. Shared nature, not cause-and-effect, justifies this merge.
